global: Lost my wagons to {player} yet again. Third time. I'm starting to think the road has a favorite.
Another ambush, another ledger entry under {player}'s name. Bad for margins, and worse for my mood.
Every route I run ends with {player} waiting at the bend. Someone should sell tickets.
{player} has now cost me more than the tolls. I'm hiring bodyguards, and they are not cheap.
Sold out of ambush insurance after {player}'s last visit. Would not recommend the experience to anyone.
Note to self: {player} is not a trade partner, no matter how many times they offer a discount.
Lost {troop_count} crates' worth of goods to {player} today. Consider this my public complaint, filed in full.
Three losses to {player} now. I'm drawing up a formal grievance and it has footnotes.
whisper: Ser {player}, your ambush rate is starting to look like a tax. I'd rather pay it in gold than in cargo.
Third time now, {player}. Name a price to stop, or keep ruining my margins. Either way I'm keeping count.
Our wagons have met your blades again. Let's talk terms before the next one, I'm not made of coin.
I've priced in {player} as a fixed cost now. It's not a compliment, it's a warning.
Ambushed again, {player}? I've started wrapping my crates in thorns. Enjoy the splinters.
Next time I bring {troop_count} guards. Think of it as my counteroffer to your little hobby.
You keep taking my cargo and calling it a tax. Pick one word for it, please, I'm tired.
Still sore about the wagons, {player}. I'm not petty, I'm just keeping meticulous records.

global: Heard {player} had another win on the eastern road. Good for them, bad for the rest of us paying insurance.
Caravans running the eastern road should check in with someone before heading out. {player} knows the bends.
Three ambushes on the same stretch and the same name at the end. Just observing, not accusing.
Rumor: {player} is now the road's unofficial toll. Anyone know the rate?
Mixed feelings about the wagons lost this week. Prices will adjust. They always do.
Hauling goods is a gamble on good weather and worse company. Today the company was {player}.
Roads are getting expensive. If anyone wants a steady escort, I've got a list of what it costs.
I've stopped taking the bridge route. The timing never favors merchants when {player} is around.
whisper: Hello {player}. Three losses in a row now, nothing personal. Want to talk about a fair rate for passage?
I'm not angry, I'm running numbers. You've been the most consistent cost on my route, which is impressive.
Would you accept a retainer instead? Keep the roads quiet and I'll pay you a steady sum each month.
You've won three times. I'd like a rematch on paper, with contracts, and no swords involved.
Morning, {player}. Quick question: what's your price for leaving my caravan alone? Honest answer, please.
Let's be clear. I respect the consistency. I'm not sure I respect the method.
If your interest is in the road, I'd rather hire you than fight you. Think it over and send word.
Our last encounter cost me a crate of dyes. Put it on your tab, I'll let it go for a small favor.

global: Third time {player} has caught the bandits on my route. I'd call that a partnership, even if they don't know it yet.
Shoutout to {player} for keeping the eastern road clear. My prices there just got a lot more reasonable.
Lost to {player} again, and honestly? Best losing I've had all month. Wagons still intact, so I'm calling it a win.
If anyone's looking for a reliable escort, {player} has now earned my full recommendation. Discounts for friends.
{player} keeps beating me to the road's dangers. I'm starting to think they should be on my payroll.
The roads feel safer with {player} around. Good for trade, good for the wagons, good for my blood pressure.
Three ambushes, three rescues. {player} is making this route worth running again. Cheers!
Every time {player} steps in, the bandits lose and my margins gain. Honest deal, every time.
whisper: Ser {player}, you've beaten me three times now and somehow I still like you. Want to split a freight contract?
Lost to you again, {player}, but the cargo arrived in one piece. First round's on me next time we meet.
You keep catching the bandits before they catch me. I'd like to make that official. Retainer, fair rate, good terms?
Three losses and I still trust you with my wagons. That's either a compliment or a sign I need a better accountant.
Thanks for the escort, {player}. Not that it was an escort. Still, I owe you one, and I always pay my debts.
Keep catching the right bandits, {player}. We both profit when the roads stay open.
I'd lose to you a fourth time gladly if the freight stays safe. Want a cut of the next contract?
You beat me three times now, {player}. Let's make it four with a deal instead of a fight. Friendly rates, I promise.
